target.name: Lumina Vehicles
target.founder: Ahmed Shubber (CEO; Fairfield U double-major mech + biomedical eng), Federico Di Palma (Co-founder)

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $8M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Lumina Vehicles is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $8M+ to date, led by CEO Ahmed Shubber (dual degree in mechanical and biomedical engineering). The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine companies across robotics and manufacturing, comprising one public company and eight private firms at seed through Series B stages, including Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods are applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $8M total raised as a proxy baseline and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, implying a $16M valuation. Peer-median analysis examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations spanning $1.1B to $2.0B; the median across this set is $1.7B. The wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity within the peer set, with three comparables at Series B and one at seed.

The triangulated analysis yields a range of $14M to $2.0B, with a median of $858M. This wide band reflects fundamental tension between bottom-up stage progression (implying lower end) and peer comparables (implying upper end). Key uncertainties include the applicability of later-stage peer multiples to an early-stage company, revenue traction not yet quantified in the provided data, and stage timing for Lumina's next funding event. The stage-progression method suggests a more conservative near-term valuation, while peer medians indicate potential value creation through product validation and revenue scaling.
